title: Formation Grammar — From Interaction to Durable Social Form
purpose: Unify Culture formation, Foundation reproduction and Below/high-control reproduction analysis without turning structural similarity into moral equivalence.
master_rule: Describe how a social form reproduces before judging what it produces. Entry, norms, authority, resources, correction, succession and exit are structural variables; harm, benefit, legality and truth require separate evidence.

fields.question: How does a person/unit become involved?
What makes participants recognize a shared role or belonging?
What repeated actions make the formation real rather than merely declared?
What rules, norms, procedures or standards coordinate behavior?
How are information, interpretation and decisions circulated?
What money, infrastructure, labor, property, data or volunteer effort sustains the form?
Where can binding decisions be made, and how concentrated or distributed is that authority?
How can error, changed conditions or internal criticism alter the system?
What happens when rules are violated? Separate ordinary governance from coercive control.
What archives, stories, records, rituals or precedent make the formation persist through time?
How do new people/units learn, inherit or obtain the capacity to continue the role?
Can participants leave, appeal, dissent, fork, replace leadership or otherwise reduce dependency?
How do new groups, chapters, projects, denominations, offices, forks or implementations emerge?
Which outside laws, publics, funders, courts, peers, audits or counterparties can constrain the formation?
Who bears effects outside the membership or declared mission?
What changes when the old form no longer works but some memory/rules survive?

independent_axes.meaning: strength of shared identity/practice; high cohesion is not inherently harmful
how much binding authority is concentrated in a person, office or small group
how much participants depend on the formation for material, social, informational or identity needs
practical social/material/legal cost of leaving; not identical to formal permission
capacity for criticism, review, reversal and learning
how information crosses internal/external boundaries; confidentiality can be legitimate
how centralized the material base is
how replaceable leaders/roles are and how succession is governed
strength and independence of outside review

route_bridge.garden_candidate: Correction, reciprocity, meaningful exit, distributed future capacity and accountable boundaries are observable.
route_bridge.strife_candidate: Role lock, enemy production, dependency, blocked correction, archive warfare or punitive exit become self-reproducing.
route_bridge.mixed: Many durable institutions contain both generative and capture-prone mechanisms at once.
route_bridge.evidence_rule: Route labels apply to episodes/mechanisms, never as permanent identities for a whole culture, religion, institution or group.
